comments.text: Gurleen Ma'am, there are two important factors which you forgot to mention. First is that some Companies like ICICI Lombard, HDFC Ergo , etc. will deny you a policy if you are above 50 and suffer from PED like Diabetes or Hypertension. Even if they do accept your request there is often a loading fee even up to 35-45 % added on to the normal premium. Second is that some companies tempt you with a low premium for the first and second year and then onwards there is a huge jacking up of premium. Some companies offer the same premium, till you make a claim (whether it is 2,3,4,5 or any number of years). But the moment you make a claim the next year's claim just skyrockets. A friend of mine took a policy from a company that had this Lock The Clock benefit. His premium was same, I think, for first three years and after this when he made a claim the premium shot up to 1.8 times the earlier premium.  Finally, if you are porting your policy to another new company and have an accumulated No Claim Bonus, some companies refuse to add this NCB in the new Policy statement as Continuity Benefit which is important if you have a PED and require cover from Day 1. The IRDA has made it mandatory to port the accumulated NCB as Continuity Benefit, but most companies fleece the new customers by giving coverage of up to only the SI of the earlier Policy. For example if you have PED  and an existing cover of Rs. 5 Lakhs SI + Rs.2.5 Lakhs NCB and are planning to port to another company for a Rs. 10 lakh policy, the new Company should give you Rs. 7.5 lakh cover from Day1 and balance Rs.2.5 lakh cover after the waiting period. But Companies shortchange, by giving only Rs.5 lakh cover from day 1 and balance Rs. 5 lakh cover till after the waiting period.
